title: The Handmaid's Tale
notes: Good writing but Atwood isn't nearly the clever poet she thinks she is. My expectations from the book were also a bit distorted; I had heard from someone who had seen the show about the titular character, in the finale, making her clever escape through some train... I was reading the novel in expectance of some strategem, but the protagonist is nothing but a mere ragdoll thrown around mostly by the schemes of those that surround her. Guess it makes more sense for the point of the novel for her to have no agency.

title: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair
notes:
7/7 music, 6/7 premise, 6/7 cases, and tolerable writing.
Nagito Komaeda is the hottest character in any anime game, and has generously offered to be embroiled in, not one of, but *the* best case I have read in detective fiction.
tagline: Live And Let The Languid World Live

title: Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony
notes:
The last case was just a middle finger to the fanbase, to be honest. Every Danganronpa had insane potential, but also something wrong with it. Danganronpa 1 with poor cases, poor characters, poor writing, and clunky ending. 2, also lacking in the ending department, unable to top-up its penultimate case.

The writer has not written enough of, anything, actually, to be making the point he seems to be trying to make. Leave good 4th wall breaking to Toby Fox, please.

Loved the cases though. Glad they hired an actual mystery writer.

title: Dweller's Empty Path
notes: I feel kind of… guilty for liking this one. It wasn’t that good… but it felt really good. The ending was sudden, though, very lacklustre, and I hated the generic “heroes” quest, even if it was meant as satire. But there was something about it... the subtle hopelessness? Treated as... ordinary. I don't know. I felt it just helping me, a bit.
tagline: A game by Temmie Chang.

title: Foundation
notes: I have heard the show is better. Full disclaimer, I only read the first book, and I wouldn't recommend it. Every protagonist of each act is the same, hard, male, and every antagonist is tricked in some way, and these tricks are *not* consistent with each other. The book did have its moments with politics, however. Everything else was either bad (worldbuiling, characterization) or mid (writing).
